title: What to expect in the emergency room
what: The emergency department is the part of a hospital where the ambulance brings you, or you come yourself with an urgent problem. You are examined there, and a decision is made about admission.
why: For sudden pain, an injury, a high fever, or when an ambulance has brought you to hospital.
duration: usually from 1 to several hours, depending on tests and how busy it is
tell_doctor: What happened, and when it started
What you already took at home

prepare.title: Documents
prepare.text: Keep your ID and health insurance card or medical record in one place at home, so you can grab them quickly.

prepare.title: Medicines
prepare.text: Bring a list of your medicines, or the packs themselves.

prepare.title: Someone with you
prepare.text: If possible, have a family member with you.

bring: Discharge papers, if you have them
steps: You are registered and briefly asked about the problem
A nurse checks your blood pressure, pulse, and temperature
The sickest patients are seen first, so the queue is not by arrival time
A doctor examines you and orders blood tests, an X-ray, or an ultrasound
Based on the results, you go home or are admitted to a ward
feel: Waiting can be long. It does not mean you have been forgotten
If you get worse while waiting, tell a nurse right away
after: If you are sent home, ask for a discharge summary and advice
If you are admitted, you will be taken to the ward
red_flags: If you get worse while waiting, with severe pain, trouble breathing, or feeling faint: tell a nurse right away

faq.q: Why was someone who came later seen first?
faq.a: In the emergency department, those who are sicker are seen first. This is done to save the most serious cases.

faq.q: Can I come without an ambulance?
faq.a: Usually yes, if your condition allows. Check which hospital handles your problem.

reminders.text: Keep your ID and medicine list in one place, in case you need to go to hospital urgently.
